input.sourceText: In order to facilitate appropriate utilization of the shared workshop facilities, consideration should be given to the difference between the dust extractor and the room ventilation system. The dust extractor collects sawdust at the tool. The room ventilation brings in outdoor air. Because the two systems serve different purposes, turn on the extractor before cutting even if the ventilation is already running. If the extractor stops during a cut, stop the tool and tell the workshop supervisor.
input.requirements: Explain this to someone who has never used the studio. Keep the equipment names and safety limits.

Editing example (conversational)
Source: For the purposes of returning borrowed equipment, please note that keys can be left at reception after the equipment has been checked in. If reception is closed, keep the keys until it reopens.
Weak revision: Regarding the return of borrowed equipment, please be aware that you can leave keys at reception after the equipment is checked in. If reception is closed, keep the keys until it reopens.
Effective revision: Once the borrowed equipment has been checked in, you can leave the keys at reception. If reception is closed, hold on to them until it reopens.
Overreach: Leave the keys at reception any time. This drops the check-in condition and the exception for a closed desk.

Target style: CONVERSATIONAL. Explain directly in accessible language. Keep necessary terms and the author's relationship to the reader.
Editing depth: RESTRUCTURE. Split or combine paragraphs and reorder independent information where helpful. Preserve chronology, causal direction and the action governed by each condition.
Explicit requirements in the user JSON override style, depth and language defaults within the meaning and quotation safeguards.
polishedText: The dust extractor and the room ventilation system do different jobs, so don't treat one as a substitute for the other. The dust extractor collects sawdust right at the tool. The room ventilation brings in outdoor air. Because they serve different purposes, turn on the extractor before you start cutting, even if the ventilation is already running. If the extractor stops during a cut, stop the tool and tell the workshop supervisor.
